newsitem.title: UK: Conoco Europe's most sophisticated refiner - WoodMac.
newsitem.headline: Conoco Europe's most sophisticated refiner - WoodMac.

text.p: Conoco Inc has by far the most sophisticated refining system in Europe while British Petroleum Co Plc has the least complex of any major, analysts Wood Mackenzie said in a survey on Thursday.

Conoco's Humber refinery had a configuration more typical of an American refiner and was a major cash flow generator for Conoco Europe, the survey of refinery configuration carried in the consultancy's Downstream Oil Review for 1996 said.

Conoco's superiority stemmed from the inclusion of an aromatic extraction and hydroalkylation unit for beneze production at Humber and improvement at Karlsruhe due to the installation of a new hydrotreater.

"Neste, DEA Mineraloel AG and PetroFina also score well, PetroFina having significantly improved its position with the addition of the new residue desulphurisation units at the Antwerp refinery in September 1994," the report said.
The report noted, however, that only a relatively small number of refiners appeared to be either significantly advantaged or disadvantaged in terms of refinery sophistication.

BP was the lowest ranking of the majors -- 25 out of a total of 30 refiners surveyed -- with "relatively poor refining assets, a consequence of a historically low level of capital spending in refining", the report.
Wood Mackenzie said BP's status would not alter much following the merger of its European downstream operations with those of Mobil Corp.

A separate section giving an octane "index" measuring octane capability said Conoco, Gulf Oil and Texaco were ahead of the pack in improving gasoline quality, in Conoco's case because of its sophisticated Humber plant.

Texaco and Gulf are joint owners of the Pembroke Cracking Company, which operates the largest catalytic cracker complex in Europe. Total's position had improved steadily since 1987 as a result of investment in new octane capacity.

The report noted that the installation of octane capacity increased not only the quality of European gasoline but also the absolute volume of gasoline output, a development that in combination with other factors had severely depressed prices.
It noted that this "dramatic" development mean that those without significant octane capacity now had no incentive to install it.

It added: "On the other hand, those companies with a strong octane capacity almost all have significant gasoline surpluses. With only modest gasoline growth forecast in the medium term these surpluses have become a strategic weakness for several companies."

The report, citing 1995 figures, added that five companies had an overall product deficit in Europe, driven mainly by large gas oil and diesel oil sales. These were Conoco, BP, Norsk Hydro, Mobile and Kuwait Petroleum International (KPI).
